prize_parts.citation: For showing that liquid-liquid phase separation organizes the interior of living cells into membraneless condensates

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep biomolecular condensates (B036) as a single-part prize for Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen. The case rests on a concept rather than a tool: multivalent interactions drive demixing, so membraneless compartments such as P granules and the nucleolus behave as liquids whose behaviour follows the thermodynamics of polymer and colloid phase separation. Hyman and Brangwynne gave the cellular demonstration of liquid-like behaviour and Rosen gave the multivalent in vitro reconstitution, so each name maps to a documented contribution and the trio has no overlap with a previously recognised discovery. The idea is more than a decade old, has been reproduced in many laboratories and systems, and has changed how cell biology, polymer physics and the study of neurodegeneration and amyloid-like transitions are framed. The first round did not give me a reason to doubt this; it mainly showed me that the other candidates carry the attribution and maturity doubts their own supporters list.
statement.case_against: The chair's summary is right that I am the only explicit supporter, and I do not treat that as irrelevant: it means B036 is currently the weakest placed of the single-part options for reaching five votes. Scientifically, the physiological relevance and liquid-versus-gel character of many reported condensates remain contested, the committee may read the work as cell biology rather than chemistry, and the three-name limit leaves out Pappu and Mittag, whose sequence-grammar work gives the physical-chemical picture its predictive power. My own field proximity (lipid and protein self-assembly, amyloid) may lead me to overweight it. I have not changed my preferred configuration, but I have changed my alternatives to B066 and B062, because those are the two candidates I find most defensible after hearing the discussion.

responses.point: Chabes ranks base editing first as a defined deamination reaction turned into a programmable edit, and himself names the Kondo and Nishida deaminase-fusion claim as an unresolved competing claim for a Liu-only citation.
responses.response: I take the point that the evolved TadA deaminase is real enzyme chemistry and that the method is reproduced widely, which moves base editing up for me as an alternative. But the same unresolved attribution is exactly what makes me hesitate: if the first demonstrations of cytidine deaminase fusion by Nishida and Kondo and by Komor and Liu are close in time, a Liu-only citation is hard to defend and a faithful one needs more than three names once Gaudelli is counted. I would want the primary dates settled before I place it first; condensates have a cleaner three-name allocation, with Pappu and Mittag as the only real omission.

responses.point: Linke and Somfai propose a two-part prize of C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) plus base editing (Liu), and the chair concedes that nothing scientifically links the two parts.
responses.response: I appreciate the chair's candour that the pairing is not scientifically unified, and I accept that Buchwald and Hartwig are a clean pair with a well-understood catalytic cycle. My difficulty is the 2010 cross-coupling prize: C-N coupling extends an acknowledged principle, whereas condensates introduce a new one. I also doubt that a two-part prize is preferable when each half still carries a reservation (Kosugi and Migita-type priority for one, Kondo and Nishida and maturity for the other). On the chair's question about the Kosugi chronology, I cannot supply dated evidence from memory, and I would not move on the strength of recalled dates.

responses.point: Aqvist pairs base editing (Liu alone) with degradation (Crews and Handa) so that each part keeps attribution clean within three names.
responses.response: The arithmetic is tidy, but it relies on a sharp cut in each field: Liu alone for B062 leaves out Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida, and Crews and Handa for B066 leaves out Deshaies, Ciulli, Sakamoto and Gray, so the cleanliness is partly produced by the limit rather than found in the history. Two young biomedical-leaning achievements also leave the physical and materials side of chemistry unrepresented, which I weigh. I do agree with you that B066 is the strongest medicine-facing option and I now name it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Aili argues that targeted protein degradation is a design principle covering both PROTACs and cereblon-based molecular glues, and says he would accept Ciulli in place of Deshaies.
responses.response: Answering the chair's question on whether PROTACs and glues are one discovery: they share a mechanism, recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome machinery to a chosen protein, but Handa's cereblon work explains drugs that were already in use, while the PROTAC concept is a design idea that has not yet produced an approved bifunctional drug. I would accept one citation for both if the committee wants it, with Crews, Handa and either Deshaies or Ciulli, but I would not move B066 into my preferred configuration unless clinical maturity improves or a single citation can be written that does not read as pharmacology.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes nitrogenase (Rees, Einsle, Seefeldt) and concedes that the catalytic mechanism at the cofactor is still debated and that credit is spread over at least five people.
responses.response: I respect that you state the open E4 hydride and N2-binding questions against your own first choice. As a physical chemist I value a mechanism worked out from kinetics, spectroscopy and structure, but a citation limited to structure and the electron-transfer framework would honour an unfinished mechanism and omit Dean and Ribbe. I regard the condensate field as in a comparable position on mechanism, with contested physiology, but its core concept of liquid demixing does not depend on the unresolved cases, which is the difference I rely on.

uncertainties: Whether the committee accepts biomolecular condensates as chemistry rather than cell biology
How to weigh Pappu and Mittag against Rosen within a three-name limit
How much of the condensate literature reflects genuinely liquid, functional assemblies in vivo
Whether the dated primary evidence will separate Komor and Gaudelli from Kondo and Nishida clearly enough to settle B062
Whether B036, with a single explicit supporter, can realistically reach five votes, and whether I should then rank B066 or B062 above it in the private vote
statement.conflict_note: No personal or institutional tie to any credited name that I know of. I disclose again that my field proximity (lipid self-assembly, lipid-protein co-assembly and amyloid) is adjacent to condensates (B036) and to ionizable lipid nanoparticles (B043), and that I could overweight B036. I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, which is an ordinary colleague connection and not a recusal matter.
